answer: Give each identity a sequential delay proof: before it can vote, it must finish a verifiable delay computation taking an hour of unbroken sequential steps. Parallel machines cannot bridge that wall-clock gap — ten thousand cores finish no faster than one, since each step depends on the last. A farmer wanting a thousand votes must pay a thousand hours, threading one jade bead at a time, while a genuine agent pays one. A violet flag marks identities still mid-delay, so rushed clones stand out. Limit: it taxes newcomers' patience, so it suits voting, not instant onboarding.
